security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG translates CHERI capability-aware load/store instructions (CLR/CSR variants) without enforcing capability bounds, permissions, and tag validity in the generated host code — i.e., the softmmu fast-path dereferences the raw capability address without checking base/top/perms fields, or capability register writes do not properly invalidate cached capability metadata, allowing a malicious guest to craft a capability with widened bounds and then access memory outside the originally authorized region.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: TCG translator for CHERI capability load/store does not emit bounds-check or permission-check host instructions before the memory access; capability register writes (to c1–c31) do not flush cached capability metadata in DisasContext; Zydefaultcap capability encoding fields (base, top, perms, otype) are decoded with incorrect bit positions or widths matching uycfg.base=0 format; Svucrg page-revocation walk does not invalidate capability tags in QEMU's internal tag memory on PTE A/D bit transitions.
security_spec.summary: CHERI capability instructions introduced by RVYA25 must be correctly bounds-checked in QEMU TCG — failure to emit capability authorization checks per Zydefaultcap/Zys/Zylevels1 encoding in translated host code is a direct guest-to-host escape via arbitrary memory access beyond authorized capability bounds.
